questions.answer: I applied through Samskipnaden and was allotted a room, but overall, very few people actually got a place to stay through Samskipnaden. I recommend looking for private options simultaneously.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everything is close to each other in Tromsø, so it is not a problem to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had many, many problems in my communication with one of the mobility staff from UiT. He seemed very confused and I was close to being admitted to a course on engineering even though I am a political science student. I was only able to reverse that because I, after a long time, was able to come in contact with someone else than him. Most of the other Danish people up here also found him very confusing and spent large amounts of time communicating with him because he kept on confusing people with rather strange decisions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was relatively straight forward, but you need to take a good look at the available courses, as I found several courses when I actually got to UiT that I had not seen when I applied.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Communication with the mobility department. As I said, this was the primary challenge for me, as the specific staff member often gave incomplete and not useful answers to my questions, and almost made me join a course that had absolutely no relevance for me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have problems in communicating with a specific staff member, then find someone else from the mobility department - they were much more helpful.

questions.answer: The Norwegian people are a bit introvert, but are extremely nice and warm-hearted when you get to know them. Just reach out to them!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that Norway is expensive, be prepared that the Mobility department might be hard to communicate with and ideally, you should try to get housing between the university and the city center - that is the best place.
